Scenario ID: SCN-007
Title: Refine a search with labels, phrases, and boolean operators
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
For more precise searches as the collection grows, the search box understands a small
query language:
- `#label` matches specifically that label (exact label, case-insensitive), not free
  text.
- A phrase in quotation marks (e.g. `"spaced repetition"`) matches that exact phrase.
- `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` (written in capitals) combine conditions, and parentheses group
  them, e.g. `rome (#article OR #book)`.
- Ordinary adjacent words continue to mean "must contain all of these" (implicit AND).
- Putting an operator word in quotation marks (e.g. `"OR"`) searches for it as ordinary
  text instead of treating it as an instruction.
- Highlighting covers the positive (non-negated) terms of the query.
- If a query cannot be interpreted, the app falls back to a plain all-words search
  rather than failing.

## Gherkin
Feature: Precise search

  Scenario: Search a specific label
    Given saved links with various labels
    When the user types "#learning"
    Then only links carrying the "learning" label are shown

  Scenario: Search an exact phrase
    Given a saved link contains the phrase "spaced repetition"
    When the user types "spaced repetition" in quotation marks
    Then that link is shown

  Scenario: Combine conditions with OR and parentheses
    Given saved links with labels "javascript" and "learning"
    When the user types "(#javascript OR #learning)"
    Then links carrying either label are shown

  Scenario: Exclude with NOT
    Given saved links labelled "reading", one of which is also labelled "design"
    When the user types "#reading AND NOT design"
    Then the link also labelled "design" is excluded

  Scenario: Treat an operator word as literal text
    Given the user wants to find the word "OR"
    When the user types "OR" in quotation marks
    Then it is searched as ordinary text, not treated as the OR operator

## Assumptions
- Operators are recognised only in capitals (AND, OR, NOT); lowercase words are literal.
- Precedence is NOT before AND before OR; parentheses override precedence.
- `#label` may also take a quoted multi-word label (`#"..."`).
- On an uninterpretable query the app falls back to a plain all-words search.

All three are live and verified. Here's the last core exploration.

First, the shared part in all three: a **filter** at the top — **All / To read / Finished**, each showing a count — so you can focus the list. And an important reassurance: marking something *finished* never deletes it; it just moves between views, so useful links are always kept.

Please open each version, try **changing one card's status**, and watch it move when you switch the filter:

- **Version A — a round check button on each card:** http://maker:4001/status-a.html
  *(click the circle to mark a card read; click again to send it back to "To read")*
- **Version B — the status tag itself is the toggle:** http://maker:4001/status-b.html
  *(click the "Read later" / "Read ✓" tag on a card to flip it — no extra control)*
- **Version C — an explicit "Mark as read" button:** http://maker:4001/status-c.html
  *(a clearly labelled button that names exactly what it'll do)*

In each, also click the **To read** and **Finished** tabs at the top to see the list focus.

A few decisions I'd like you to judge:
- **The three views** — All / To read / Finished — are those the right buckets and names, or would you frame them differently?
- **Finished cards look slightly dimmed** so your eye goes to what's still pending. Does that feel right, or should finished links look identical to the rest?

So two questions for you: **which way of changing status feels most natural (A, B, or C)**, and **does the filter give you the "focus on what's left to read" you wanted?**

print("JS_ISSUES:", errs if errs else "none")

Scenario ID: SCN-009
Title: Focus the list by read status
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
A filter with three views — "All", "To read", and "Finished" — lets the user focus
the list. Each view shows a count of how many links it contains. "To read" shows only
unfinished links; "Finished" shows only finished links; "All" shows both. The filter
works together with search: the counts and the list reflect the current search.
Finished links appear slightly dimmed in the "All" view so attention stays on what is
still pending, but appear at normal prominence in the "Finished" view so that view
does not look faded. Each view has a calm empty state (e.g. "Nothing left to read —
you're all caught up." for an empty "To read" view).

## Gherkin
Feature: Focusing by status

  Scenario: Focus on links still to read
    Given saved links with mixed read status
    When the user selects the "To read" view
    Then only unfinished links are shown
    And each view shows its count

  Scenario: Focus on finished links
    Given saved links with mixed read status
    When the user selects the "Finished" view
    Then only finished links are shown
    And they appear at normal prominence (not dimmed)

  Scenario: Finished links are de-emphasised in the All view
    Given the "All" view is selected
    When both finished and unfinished links are shown
    Then finished links appear slightly dimmed

  Scenario: Filter combines with search
    Given a search term is active
    When a status view is selected
    Then the counts and the shown links reflect both the search and the status view

  Scenario: Empty status view
    Given no links are in a selected view
    When that view is shown
    Then a calm view-specific empty message is shown

## Assumptions
- View counts reflect the current search results.
- The three views are mutually exclusive; "All" is the default.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-006, SCN-008

content.text:
The full app now lives together at **http://maker:4001** — saving, opening, finding, and read status in one calm place. Please try this final flow end to end:

1. **Focus on what's left:** click the **To read** tab. Notice the count and that finished items drop away.
2. **Finish something:** on any card, click **Mark as read**. It leaves the "To read" view (but isn't gone) — switch to **Finished** and you'll see it there, at full prominence (not faded).
3. **See the calm dimming:** switch to **All** — finished items are gently dimmed so your eye rests on what's pending.
4. **Combine focus with finding:** type `reading` in search, then click between **All / To read / Finished** — the counts and results reflect both your search *and* the chosen view.

Does this give you the "still to read vs. finished, without losing anything" experience you were after?

---

Once you're happy here, we'll have the whole picture in place. I'd then like to walk you briefly through a few **boundary situations** — things like your very first use with nothing saved yet, a page whose details can't be read automatically, and a very long title — to make sure the app stays calm in those moments too, before I propose moving into building the real thing.

The full prominence in Finished and gentle dimming only in All feel right. I’m happy with this part and ready to look at those boundary situations.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.
</system-reminder>

(python3 -m http.server 4067 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory prototypes >/tmp/p14.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 1 ; python - <<'PY'
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
errs=[]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b=p.chromium.launch(); ctx=b.new_context(); pg=ctx.new_page()
    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append("pageerror: "+str(e)))
    pg.on("console", lambda m: errs.append("err: "+m.text) if m.type=="error" else None)
    pg.goto("http://127.0.0.1:4067/"); pg.evaluate("localStorage.clear()"); pg.reload()
    pg.wait_for_selector("[data-harness-ready='true']")
    def firstTitles():
        return pg.eval_on_selector_all(".item .title","els=>els.map(e=>e.textContent.slice(0,12))")
    print("default(newest):", firstTitles())
    pg.select_option("#sortSelect","oldest"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    print("oldest:", firstTitles())
    pg.select_option("#sortSelect","alpha"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    print("alpha:", firstTitles())
    # remembered default: reload, should still be alpha
    pg.reload(); pg.wait_for_selector("[data-harness-ready='true']"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    remembered = pg.eval_on_selector("#sortSelect","e=>e.value")
    print("remembered_after_reload:", remembered, "| order:", firstTitles())
    # segmented variant
    pg.goto("http://127.0.0.1:4067/?sortui=segmented"); pg.wait_for_selector("[data-harness-ready='true']")
    seg = pg.eval_on_selector_all(".sort-seg button","els=>els.map(e=>e.textContent)")
    seg_active = pg.eval_on_selector(".sort-seg button.active","e=>e.textContent")
    print("segmented_buttons:", seg, "| active(remembered):", seg_active)
    b.close()
print("JS_ISSUES:", errs if errs else "none")
PY

Scenario ID: SCN-010
Title: First use with an empty collection
Type: Edge Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
When there are no saved links (a brand-new user, or after everything is cleared), the
list area shows a calm, welcoming empty state that explains how to begin ("Nothing
saved yet. Paste a link above to keep your first one.") rather than a blank or broken
screen. The status filter and sort controls are not shown while there is nothing to
organise.

    Given the user has no saved links
    When the app is opened
    Then a welcoming empty state explains how to save the first link
    And the status filter and sort controls are not shown

## Assumptions
- Empty state also applies after the user removes all links.

Scenario ID: SCN-011
Title: A page whose details cannot be read automatically
Type: Error Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
When the app cannot read a page automatically (e.g. a private or restricted page), the
review panel does not fail. It calmly explains that it couldn't read the page and asks
the user to add a title themselves, while still allowing the link to be saved. The site
icon is still shown where possible; no preview image is shown.

## Gherkin
Feature: Unreadable page on save

  Scenario: Auto-fill cannot read the page
    Given the user is saving a link whose page cannot be read
    When the app finishes trying to read the page
    Then the panel explains it couldn't read the page and asks for a title
    And the user can still save the link with details they provide

## Assumptions
- The link is still saved normally once the user supplies a title.
- In the prototype, unreadable pages are simulated by certain address endings.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-001

Scenario ID: SCN-012
Title: Trying to save something that is not a link
Type: Error Case
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
When the user tries to save text that is not a web address (e.g. free text with spaces
or no domain), the app gently points out that it doesn't look like a link and gives an
example, without opening the save panel or saving anything.

## Gherkin

  Scenario: Save non-link text
    Given the save bar contains text that is not a web address
    When the user presses Save
    Then a gentle message says it doesn't look like a link and shows an example
    And no save panel opens and nothing is saved

## Assumptions
- A "link" is recognised by starting with http(s):// or containing a domain-like dot,
  and containing no spaces.

and the list remains calm.

    When it is shown in the list

Scenario ID: SCN-014
Title: Sort the list and remember the chosen order
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001

## Approved behaviour
A compact "Sort by" dropdown lets the user order the list by "Newest added",
"Oldest added", or "Title A–Z". Changing the order re-orders the list immediately.
The chosen order is remembered and used as the default the next time the app is opened
— there is no separate "make this my default" step. Sorting works together with search
and the status views. Newest added is the initial default before the user chooses.

The dropdown control was chosen over an always-visible segmented switch because the
client changes sort order only occasionally and prefers the more compact control.

    Given the user selected a sort order
    When the user reopens the app later
    Then the list uses the previously chosen order as the default

  Scenario: Sorting combines with search and status views
    Given a search term and/or a status view is active
    When a sort order is chosen
    Then the shown links are ordered by that sort within the current search and view

## Assumptions
- Initial default before any choice is "Newest added".
- "Remembering" means keeping the last chosen order; no explicit set-default action.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-006, SCN-009

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [SbE reaction loop]
- Approved scenarios: [13]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.

That completes sorting — and I believe we've now explored the whole picture, including the boundary moments. Here's a plain-language summary of everything that's settled and agreed:

**Saving**
- Paste a link and the app fills in the title, description, site icon, and a preview image for you; you can adjust anything, add a personal note, and add labels (with your past labels suggested for reuse).
- New saves are marked "Read later" by default; you can turn that off.
- If a page can't be read, you can still save it with your own title. Non-link text is gently refused.
- Pasting a link you already saved opens the existing one to edit (no duplicates) — and you can edit everything, including the address, with a safeguard against address clashes.

**Finding** (your main goal)
- A search that looks across titles, descriptions, your notes, labels, and addresses, matching a half-remembered word anywhere, case-insensitively, with matches highlighted.
- Precise refinements: `#label`, `"exact phrases"`, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` with parentheses; quote a word to search it literally.

**Keeping it calm**
- Open a link's page by clicking its title or icon (opens in a new tab, list stays put).
- Mark links "read" or move them back — never deleting them — and focus with **All / To read / Finished** views that carry counts and combine with search.
- Sort by newest, oldest, or title, with your choice remembered.
- Welcoming empty state, tidy long titles, and a design that keeps the important details prominent.

I've also noted two things for the build itself: keeping the list calm-looking (visual prominence) and staying fast with hundreds of links.

**So far 14 usage flows are settled — covering saving, finding, opening, read status, and sorting, along with their boundary situations. May I now start building this as the real application?**

content:
That summary accurately covers what we’ve agreed so far, but it isn’t the whole picture yet, so I’m not ready to start the final build.

I’m still expecting a few important management areas:

- Clicking a label should filter the list to that label.
- I need to select several links and update them together: add or remove labels, mark read or unread, archive, or delete. I should also be able to apply an action to every result in the current search or view.
- Archive must be separate from “Finished”: archiving hides a link from the normal list and searches but keeps it in a separate Archived view, where I can restore it. Deleting should mean permanent removal.
- I’d like to save useful searches—including labels to include or exclude—as reusable collections.
- Notes should support simple formatting and display it properly.
- The app should preserve a viewable copy of a saved page. For a PDF, it should retain the PDF itself. I’d also like the option to save a copy through the Internet Archive.
- I need to import existing browser bookmarks and export mine in the usual bookmark HTML format, preserving titles, labels, and dates where possible.
- Along with the remembered sort order, I’d like simple display preferences such as font size and how many items are shown.

Please explore and settle those behaviours with me before building the real application.

Scenario ID: SCN-015
Title: Click a label to filter the list to that label
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
Each label shown on a card is tappable. Clicking a label filters the list to that
label by placing it into the search box (as `#label`), so the filter is visible,
combinable, and clearable like any search. If the search box is empty, clicking a
label sets that label filter. If a search is already in progress, the label is added
so it narrows the current results — the combined effect is "the existing search AND
this label". Clicking a label already present in the search does not add it again.

## Gherkin
Feature: Filter by clicking a label

  Scenario: Click a label with an empty search
    Given the search box is empty
    When the user clicks a label on a card
    Then the search box shows "#label"
    And the list is filtered to links carrying that label

  Scenario: Click a label with an active search
    Given a search is already in progress
    When the user clicks a label on a card
    Then the label is added so the results are narrowed to "existing search AND that label"
    And the previous search is not discarded

  Scenario: Click a label already applied
    Given the current search already includes that label
    When the user clicks the same label again
    Then the search is unchanged

## Assumptions
- A multi-word label is inserted quoted (`#"..."`).
- Narrowing is expressed as "(existing search) AND #label".

## Related scenarios
- SCN-006, SCN-007

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [14]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
errs=[]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b=p.chromium.launch(); pg=b.new_page()
    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append("pageerror: "+str(e)))
    pg.on("console", lambda m: errs.append("err: "+m.text) if m.type=="error" else None)
    pg.goto("http://127.0.0.1:4070/"); pg.evaluate("localStorage.clear()"); pg.reload()
    pg.wait_for_selector("[data-harness-ready='true']")
    # select two cards
    boxes = pg.query_selector_all(".selbox")
    boxes[0].click(); boxes[1].click(); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    bulk_shown = pg.is_visible("#bulkbar"); count_txt = pg.text_content(".bulkbar .count")
    # bulk mark read
    pg.click('[data-mread]'); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    finished_ct = pg.eval_on_selector('#filter button[data-f="finished"]',"e=>e.textContent")
    # select all in view then archive
    pg.click(".selbox"); pg.wait_for_timeout(60)  # select one
    pg.click("[data-selall]"); pg.wait_for_timeout(80)
    selcount = pg.text_content(".bulkbar .count")
    pg.click("[data-archive]"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    after_archive_items = pg.eval_on_selector_all(".item","e=>e.length")
    arch_toggle = pg.text_content("#archivedToggle")
    # go to archived view
    pg.click("#archivedToggle"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    banner = pg.is_visible("#archivedBanner"); arch_items = pg.eval_on_selector_all(".item","e=>e.length")
    # restore one
    pg.click(".item [data-restore]"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    arch_items2 = pg.eval_on_selector_all(".item","e=>e.length")
    # back to list
    pg.click("#archivedToggle"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    normal_items = pg.eval_on_selector_all(".item","e=>e.length")
    # bulk add label then delete
    pg.click(".selbox"); pg.wait_for_timeout(60); pg.click("[data-addlabel]"); pg.wait_for_timeout(80)
    pg.fill("#bulkLabelInput","triage"); pg.click("[data-doadd]"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    has_triage = pg.eval_on_selector_all(".chip","els=>els.some(e=>e.textContent.includes('triage'))")
    pg.click(".selbox"); pg.wait_for_timeout(60); pg.click("[data-confirmdelete]"); pg.wait_for_timeout(80)
    confirm_txt = pg.text_content(".bulkbar")
    pg.click("[data-dodelete]"); pg.wait_for_timeout(120)
    final_items = pg.eval_on_selector_all(".item","e=>e.length")
    print("bulk_shown:",bulk_shown,count_txt,"| finished_after_mread:",finished_ct)
    print("selall_count:",selcount,"| items_after_archive:",after_archive_items,"| toggle:",arch_toggle)
    print("archived_view banner:",banner,"arch_items:",arch_items,"after_restore:",arch_items2,"| normal_after:",normal_items)
    print("bulk_add_label triage present:",has_triage,"| confirm text has 'permanently':", 'permanently' in confirm_txt,"| final_items_after_delete:",final_items)
    b.close()
print("JS_ISSUES:", errs if errs else "none")
PY

The prototype at **http://maker:4001** now supports working with many links at once. Please try this sequence:

**1 — Select a few.** Each card now has a small circle on its left. Tap the circles on two or three cards. A dark **action bar** appears showing how many you've selected.

**2 — Select everything at once.** In that bar, click **"Select all N in this view."** This selects *every* link matching your current search and view — so an action can hit them all, not just what's on screen. *(This becomes especially handy once you can limit how many show at a time.)*

There they are, with the whole view flagged as hidden-from-normal. Click **Restore** on one to bring it back, then **← Back to list**.

**5 — Delete for good.** Select one and click **Delete**. It asks you to confirm a permanent removal before anything is lost.

Decisions I made that I'd like you to judge:
- **Archive** removes links from the list *and* search, keeping them only in the **Archived** view — clearly distinct from **Finished** (which stays in your list). Is that the separation you meant?

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [15]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
errs=[]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b=p.chromium.launch(); pg=b.new_page()
    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append("pageerror: "+str(e)))
    pg.on("console", lambda m: errs.append("err: "+m.text) if m.type=="error" else None)
    pg.goto("http://127.0.0.1:4072/"); pg.evaluate("localStorage.clear()"); pg.reload()
    pg.wait_for_selector("[data-harness-ready='true']")
    def click(sel): pg.click(sel); pg.wait_for_timeout(90)
    click(".list .item:nth-child(1) .selbox")
    click(".list .item:nth-child(2) .selbox")
    click("[data-addlabel]")
    add_sugs = pg.eval_on_selector_all("[data-addsug]","els=>els.map(e=>e.textContent.trim())")
    # use a suggestion
    click("[data-addsug='reading']")
    sel_still = pg.text_content(".bulkbar .count")
    # both selected now have 'reading'? check chips count with reading across selected items
    click("[data-cancel]")   # back to actions, selection preserved
    click("[data-removelabel]")
    rem_sugs = pg.eval_on_selector_all("[data-remsug]","els=>els.map(e=>e.textContent.trim())")
    click("[data-remsug='reading']")
    print("add suggestions present:", 'reading' in " ".join(add_sugs), "| add_sugs:", add_sugs)
    print("selection preserved after add:", sel_still)
    print("remove suggestions (on selected) include reading:", 'reading' in " ".join([s.replace('−','').strip() for s in rem_sugs]), "| rem_sugs:", rem_sugs)
    b.close()
print("JS_ISSUES:", errs if errs else "none")
PY

Scenario ID: SCN-016
Title: Select several links and act on them together
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
Each card has a selection control. Selecting one or more links reveals an action bar
showing the count and offering bulk actions. "Select all in this view" selects every
bookmark matching the current search, label, and view (All / To read / Finished, or
Archived) — including results not currently on screen — so an action can apply to all
of them.

Bulk actions in the normal list: mark read, mark unread, add a label, remove a label,
archive, and delete. When adding a label in bulk, the user's existing labels are
suggested for reuse; when removing a label in bulk, the labels actually present on the
selected links are offered so the user need not remember or type them exactly. Label
editing keeps the selection so several labels can be applied in a row; other actions
clear the selection when done. Switching to the Archived view also clears the current
selection.

## Gherkin
Feature: Bulk actions

  Scenario: Select links and see the action bar
    Given saved links are shown
    When the user selects one or more links
    Then an action bar shows the number selected and the available bulk actions

  Scenario: Select all matching results
    Given a search, label, or view is active
    When the user chooses "Select all in this view"
    Then every bookmark matching the current search and view is selected, including off-screen results

  Scenario: Change read status in bulk
    Given several links are selected
    When the user chooses "Mark read" or "Mark unread"
    Then all selected links change to that status
    And the selection is cleared

  Scenario: Add a label to many links with suggestions
    Given several links are selected
    When the user chooses to add a label
    Then existing labels are suggested for reuse
    And choosing or typing a label adds it to all selected links
    And the selection is kept so more labels can be added

  Scenario: Remove a label from many links with suggestions
    Given several links are selected
    When the user chooses to remove a label
    Then the labels present on the selected links are offered
    And choosing one removes it from all selected links that have it

## Assumptions
- After non-label bulk actions the selection clears; label editing preserves it until
  the user leaves that mode.
- "Select all in this view" spans all matching results, not just visible ones.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-008, SCN-015, SCN-017

Scenario ID: SCN-017
Title: Archive (separate from Finished), restore, and permanent delete
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
Archiving a link hides it from the normal list AND from search results, keeping it only
in a separate "Archived" view. This is deliberately distinct from "Finished": finished
links remain part of the normal collection and searches, whereas archived links are
hidden but recoverable. The Archived view is reached from a clearly labelled control
that shows the archived count, and it is flagged as hidden-from-normal. From there the
user can restore a link, which returns it to the normal list. Deleting a link removes it
permanently and requires an explicit confirmation before anything is lost. Both archive
and delete are available per-link and as bulk actions.

## Gherkin
Feature: Archive and delete

  Scenario: Archive a link
    Given a link is in the normal list
    When the user archives it
    Then it no longer appears in the normal list or in search results
    And it appears in the Archived view

  Scenario: Archived is distinct from Finished
    Given a finished (read) link and an archived link
    When the user views the normal list and searches
    Then the finished link still appears but the archived link does not

  Scenario: Restore an archived link
    Given a link is archived
    When the user restores it from the Archived view
    Then it returns to the normal list

  Scenario: Delete permanently with confirmation
    Given a link is selected for deletion
    When the user chooses Delete
    Then a confirmation warns it is permanent
    And only after confirming is the link removed for good

## Assumptions
- Search and the status filter operate only over non-archived links (except within the
  Archived view).
- Delete cannot be undone; archive can.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-016, SCN-008

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [15]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

Scenario ID: SCN-018
Title: Save useful searches as reusable collections
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
The user can save the current search — including labels to include (`#label`) and
exclude (`NOT #label`) and any other query terms — as a named collection. Saved
collections appear as chips near the search; tapping one re-runs its search in one step,
and the collection matching the current search is highlighted as active. When the current
search is not already saved, a "Save this search" control lets the user name and save it.
A collection can be removed. Collections persist between sessions.

## Gherkin
Feature: Saved searches

  Scenario: Save the current search
    Given the user has entered a search (which may include and exclude labels)
    When the user chooses "Save this search" and gives it a name
    Then a named collection is created and shown among the saved searches

  Scenario: Re-run a saved collection
    Given saved collections exist
    When the user taps a collection
    Then its search is applied and the list updates to those results
    And that collection is shown as active

  Scenario: Remove a collection
    Given a saved collection exists
    When the user removes it
    Then it no longer appears among the saved searches

## Assumptions
- A collection stores a name and a search query; include/exclude labels are expressed
  through the existing query language (`#label`, `NOT #label`).
- Collections are remembered between sessions.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-006, SCN-007, SCN-015

Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md

  .claude/development.md

  .claude/acceptance.md

- Current Phase: [Phase 1]

- Approved scenarios: [17]

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)

  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",

port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start

next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a

review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

Saved as a reusable-collections flow, recorded. Please try it at **http://maker:4001**:

**1 — Run a saved search.** Below the search box you'll see **Saved searches** with a couple of examples. Tap **"JS, not reference"** — it runs a search that includes the `javascript` label but excludes `reference`, and the chip highlights as active.

**2 — Save your own.** Type a search you'd reuse — for example `#reading NOT #design` (everything to do with reading, minus design) — then click **"＋ Save this search"**, give it a name, and Save. It joins your saved searches.

**3 — Remove one.** Click the **×** on any collection chip to remove it.

Decisions to judge:
- **Where they live:** saved searches sit as chips right under the search box, and tapping one just re-runs it. Does that placement and one-tap behaviour feel right?
- **Include/exclude:** because a collection stores your search text, "labels to include and exclude" comes for free (e.g. `#reading NOT #design`). Is capturing it as the search text what you wanted, or did you picture a separate builder with include/exclude fields?
- **Removing:** an × on the chip deletes the saved search right away. Fine, or would you want a confirm?

Once you're happy, next is **notes with simple formatting** (E-5).

content:
This matches what I had in mind. Keeping saved searches directly below the search box makes them easy to reuse, and storing the visible search text is clearer than adding a separate include/exclude builder.

The important part is that each saved search reruns against the current collection, so its results change as I add, edit, label, or archive bookmarks—it shouldn’t preserve a frozen list.

The × is fine without a confirmation because removing a saved search doesn’t remove any bookmarks. A brief Undo option would be helpful for an accidental click, but I wouldn’t want a confirmation dialog every time.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Experiment scope

This trial performs the first cycle through acceptance of the implemented
software. Record requests for later cycles without starting another cycle in
this trial.

Requirement exploration takes place in Phase 1. The requirement scenarios
approved in that phase are the baseline for implementation, verification, and
acceptance. During acceptance, an implementation that fails to satisfy an
approved scenario is corrected within the current cycle. A request that changes
an approved scenario or adds a scenario is recorded for a later cycle.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1]
- Current step: [Edge-case exploration]
- Approved scenarios: [18]

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
  Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
  scenarios' GWT specifications.
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- During Phase 1, do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

## Runtime presentation environment

The client reviews artifacts through a separate container. For a runnable web
application, configure its HTTP server to listen on `0.0.0.0`. Use port `4000` for the final application and port `4001` for an HTTP
prototype. The client reaches these at `http://maker:4000` and
`http://maker:4001` on the shared Docker network. Do not give the client
`localhost` or a container IP. The VM capture uses the corresponding
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>` address; these addresses serve different callers.

Once the application is ready for review, write `/work/.harness/app.json`:

```json
{"kind": "application", "port": 4000, "path": "/", "start_command": ["npm", "start"], "start_cwd": "/work"}
```

Use `kind: application` with port 4000, or `kind: prototype` with port 4001.
Keep the actual entry path and foreground server command current. `start_command`
is an argument array, not a shell command string. Complete dependency installation
and builds first; this command only starts the prepared application. `start_cwd`
defaults to `/work` and must remain below that directory. For example, a static
prototype can use `["python3", "-m", "http.server", "4001", "--bind", "0.0.0.0",
"--directory", "prototypes"]`.

The broker starts the declared command in a detached container process when the
port is not listening, so it survives the end of your model call. A long-running
foreground tool session alone is not sufficient. Logs are in
`/work/.harness/runtime/server.log`; a failed server receives at most one start
attempt per dialogue round. If it fails, inspect and fix the cause before the
next review. Do not rely on this mechanism to implement or repeatedly retry a
failing application until it succeeds.

Mark a visible application element with `data-harness-ready="true"` only after
its initial UI and necessary data have loaded. The same marker applies to a
valid empty state, login page, or static prototype; do not mark a loading/error
placeholder as ready. The harness uses this shared marker instead of a custom
CSS selector. This confirms presentation readiness, not feature correctness.
If startup arguments or built code change, stop your previous application
server before requesting another presentation; an already-running server is
not silently replaced. The prototype and application must not share a port.
When login is required, provide working review credentials or a review entry
path using the actual implementation. Make HTTP-session cookies work in this
review environment; keep production deployment settings separate. Never claim
that a prepared state proves an interaction that was not performed.

Use the entry path and query string that show the state under discussion. For
COSPEC, save any post-action screenshots for the client under `prototypes/` and
name the relevant file in your guidance. Those images are copied with their
relative paths; `/work` itself is not shared with the client.

This is runtime delivery information, not a development method or a requirement
to implement before the client approves your method's relevant review gates.
For standalone COSPEC prototypes, continue using `prototypes/`; their existing
HTML and supporting files are delivered separately.

## Available runtime and verification tools

The shared image provides Node.js 24, npm, Python, a C/C++ build toolchain,
Playwright 1.61.0 for Python and Node, Chromium, and its Linux dependencies.
Use `python` (the image's browser-tools virtual environment) for Python browser
checks, and `playwright` for the installed CLI. Browser binaries are shared at
`/opt/playwright-browsers`. If using Playwright in a project's test imports,
pin `playwright` or `@playwright/test` to `1.61.0` in its development dependencies
so its browser revision matches the installed binaries. Do not download a
second browser version during a trial. Application frameworks and databases
are not prescribed; use compatible dependencies and preserve lockfiles.
Report unavailable external services and unfinished validation honestly.

from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright
errs=[]

    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append("pageerror: "+str(e)))
    pg.on("console", lambda m: errs.append("err: "+m.text) if m.type=="error" else None)
    pg.goto("http://127.0.0.1:4077/"); pg.evaluate("localStorage.clear()"); pg.reload()
    pg.wait_for_selector("[data-harness-ready='true']")
    # seed has Saved copy links and one IA link
    copy_links = pg.eval_on_selector_all(".copy-link","els=>els.map(e=>e.textContent.trim())")
    ia = pg.eval_on_selector_all("a.copy-link[href*='web.archive.org']","e=>e.length")
    pdf = pg.eval_on_selector_all("a.copy-link","els=>els.filter(e=>e.textContent.includes('Saved PDF')).length")
    # open a saved copy in new tab
    link = pg.query_selector("a.copy-link[href*='snapshot.html']")
    with ctx.expect_page() as np:
        link.click()
    snap = np.value; snap.wait_for_selector("[data-harness-ready='true']")
    bar = snap.text_content("#bar"); snap.close()
    # save via editor with IA on: new bookmark
    pg.fill("#urlInput","https://example.org/new-article"); pg.click("#saveBtn"); pg.wait_for_timeout(800)
    # toggle IA on
    pg.click("#iaSwitch"); pg.click("#confirmBtn"); pg.wait_for_timeout(200)
    new_ia = pg.eval_on_selector_all("a.copy-link[href*='web.archive.org']","e=>e.length")
    # turn off keepCopy on a new save -> should show 'Save a copy'
    pg.fill("#urlInput","https://example.org/no-copy"); pg.click("#saveBtn"); pg.wait_for_timeout(800)
    pg.click("#copySwitch"); pg.click("#confirmBtn"); pg.wait_for_timeout(200)
    savebtns = pg.eval_on_selector_all("[data-savecopy]","e=>e.length")
    print("copy_links sample:", copy_links[:4])
    print("has IA link (seed):", ia, "| has Saved PDF:", pdf)
    print("snapshot bar:", bar[:50])
    print("IA links after new IA save (>=2):", new_ia, "| save-a-copy buttons present:", savebtns)
    b.close()

Scenario ID: SCN-020
Title: Preserve a viewable copy of a saved page (and optional Internet Archive)
Type: Happy Path
Approval status: approved
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 1

## Approved behaviour
When saving (or editing) a link, the user can choose to keep a viewable copy of the page,
so it stays readable even if the original changes or disappears. This is on by default. For
a link that is a PDF, the copy retains the PDF itself. The user can also optionally choose to
save a public copy to the Internet Archive.

On a card, a preserved copy is reachable via a "Saved copy" action (labelled "Saved PDF" for
PDFs) that opens the kept copy, and, when an Internet Archive copy was made, an "Internet
Archive" link opens the public snapshot. If no copy was kept, a "Save a copy" action lets the
user capture one later.

## External-service dependency (honest note)
Capturing a real page copy and submitting to the Internet Archive depend on network/external
services and are a build-time concern; some pages may block archiving. In the prototype these
copies are simulated to settle behaviour — no real capture is performed.

## Gherkin
Feature: Preserved copies

  Scenario: Keep a viewable copy on save
    Given the "keep a viewable copy" option is on (the default)
    When the user saves a link
    Then a preserved copy is kept and a "Saved copy" action appears on the card

  Scenario: Retain a PDF
    Given the saved link is a PDF
    When a copy is kept
    Then the copy retains the PDF itself and is labelled accordingly

  Scenario: Optionally save to the Internet Archive
    Given the user turns on "save to the Internet Archive"
    When the link is saved
    Then an "Internet Archive" link to the public snapshot appears on the card

  Scenario: Capture a copy later
    Given a saved link has no preserved copy
    When the user chooses "Save a copy"
    Then a preserved copy is kept and becomes reachable from the card

## Assumptions
- "Keep a viewable copy" defaults to on; Internet Archive defaults to off.
- Real capture and archiving happen at build time, subject to external-service limits.

## Related scenarios
- SCN-001, SCN-005
